items.name: Nvidia halts AI-server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia (FT Thu 26 Nov; WSJ same day): Nvidia instructed manufacturing partners including Dell and Supermicro to stop server deliveries to the four countries for an unspecified period while it assesses whether regional partners meet US export requirements; partners have told customers 'Nvidia will not authorize their shipments'; trigger is the BIS interim final rule of 16 Nov (effective 19 Nov) requiring licences for overseas data centres that remotely supply >12m TPP of advanced chips to China/Macau-HQ companies (Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil named; existing DCs have 90 days, to ~17 Feb 2027; comment period to 19 Jan 2027); Institute for Progress estimates such remote DCs supply ~24% of China's AI compute; Nvidia booked USD 104bn of 2025 revenue (+72%) through its Singapore subsidiary (which also books part of Taiwan/China revenue); CNBC: sellers seeking buyers for thousands of B300 GPUs meant for Chinese-rented capacity; Malaysia approved MYR 123.5bn of DC/cloud investment in 9M26 (35.2% of all approved investment); Nvidia's Q4 guide (USD 130bn) assumes no China DC compute revenue; USD 32bn of neocloud agreements depend on partners obtaining financing (24/7 Wall St); no Nvidia statement in the pages read; whether the suspension is temporary 'remains unclear'
items.headline: Nvidia freezes AI-server deliveries to four Southeast Asian countries over the new US remote-access chip rule (FT/WSJ 26 Nov); Dell and Supermicro told to hold shipments; duration unspecified
items.candidate_dial: B2-capex / supplier (a supplier-side shipment PAUSE, not a capex cut - the demand is Chinese-tenant remote compute that the 16 Nov rule targets; the macro question for the orchestrator is how much of the Singapore-booked revenue (USD 104bn in 2025, part of it Taiwan/China pass-through) is at risk and whether the GPUs are re-routed to US buyers (supportive for US-chain supply) or stranded (the B300 resale reports); pairs with the late Asia DC-loan item below - the export-control channel, not the demand channel, is what is shutting AI-infra credit and shipments this week)
items.source: TrendForce news 'NVIDIA reportedly suspends AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries amid tighter US curbs' (26 Nov; FT-sourced); TechCrunch 'Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia' (26 Nov 12:03 PST; WSJ-sourced); 24/7 Wall St via Yahoo 'New US chip rule is now hitting AI data-center loans' (26 Nov 05:28 PST; rule detail)
items.note: FT and WSJ primaries not read (refused/not attempted); vlsi.kr 'Daily Silicon' (which also carried the Korea Thu close) client_error. TrendForce dates the Commerce measures 'last week'; 24/7 Wall St gives 16 Nov issued / 19 Nov effective. No shipment volumes, chip models or revenue-at-risk figure printed. Market reaction Thu: none in the US (closed); Asia Friday rallied regardless (see the Friday item).

items.name: Lenders freeze or step back from Asian AI-data-center loans tied to ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent after the 16 Nov BIS rule (Bloomberg Wed 25 Nov, citing people familiar; relayed AI Affairs 25 Nov 18:50Z and 24/7 Wall St 26 Nov): Aolani Cloud (Singapore) USD 480m loan for Nvidia GPUs at a Malaysian DC serving ByteDance - work frozen since 17 Nov, bankers at five lenders discussed withdrawing or declining, no lender formally cited the rule; Bridge Data Centers (Bain-owned; Malaysian sites serve ByteDance) seeking an upsized USD 6.6bn loan - some lenders delaying for more due diligence; Digital Halo (Malaysia) - one bank declined to join a fully underwritten USD 372m loan; GMI Cloud (Thailand DC used by Tencent) USD 300m chip loan - at least one fund left; loan had been offered at low-teens yields when first sought in September, and a proposed condition requires full early repayment if Tencent is added to a US restricted-party list; United Overseas Bank ~USD 1bn significant-risk-transfer slowed; DayOne (largest customer ByteDance) US listing plans on hold; banks struggling to find buyers for loan portions they want to sell; APAC data-centre lending grew from almost nothing in 2023 to >USD 49bn; trade lawyer Kostrzewa: 'it could be a good pause'; Nvidia interim CEO Kress (17 Nov): outlook 'considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end-customer demand'
items.headline: Bloomberg: banks freeze a USD 480m Aolani GPU loan (ByteDance tenant), delay Bridge DC's USD 6.6bn, a bank drops a USD 372m Digital Halo deal and a fund exits GMI Cloud's USD 300m (Tencent) after the new US remote-access chip rule - 'billions' of Asian AI-DC loans stalled
items.candidate_dial: A-debt / C-credit (NEAR-MISS for the hard-event class 'pulled or downsized AI-infra deal': this is lenders withdrawing from or freezing AI-infra loans - five deals, ~USD 8.7bn gross - but none was formally pulled or resized, the cause is export-control licensing risk on Chinese tenants rather than AI demand or credit appetite, and the borrowers are Chinese-tenant neoclouds outside the registered set; the orchestrator should decide whether a regulatory freeze counts; the 24/7 Wall St test is the right one: if Bridge or Aolani close once licences issue, it was a pause; if both stay stuck and Nvidia trims neocloud commitments (USD 32bn financing-contingent) at its next print, it was a pull. Companion to the Nvidia SE Asia shipment halt (26 Nov) and the only new primary-market withdrawal in the files since the selloff began)

items.name: TrendForce cuts its 2027 DRAM industry revenue forecast to USD 1.15tn (Wed 25 Nov; prior figure not printed; still +69% y/y) and 2027 NAND to ~USD 419.3bn with prices falling through an oversupplied year - the first forecast cut after its first 2027 memory-price warning ~a week earlier (NAND Q1-27 flat-to-down 5%, 19 Nov): unnamed Chinese cloud providers began scaling back 2027 orders in mid-November (GPU shortages, heavy inventories, an AI-token price war) by more than North American CSPs added; some Chinese providers have trimmed 2027 server-DRAM demand OUTSIDE long-term agreements since early October; DRAM quarterly contract-price increases to narrow and possibly level off in 2H27; phone/PC makers expected to strip storage from 2027 models; LTA coverage: Micron >75% of FY27 shipments committed, Sandisk ~half of FY27 output - 'those hold while prices flatten; the next contracts are priced into a different market'; 'NAND has no such cushion'; MU -42% from its June peak (Q4 FY26 revenue USD 54.23bn, six straight rises), Sandisk -49% in a month; HPE (24 Nov): memory/NAND constraints last at least into 2H28; next test MU FQ1 17 Dec
items.headline: TrendForce (25 Nov) cuts 2027 DRAM revenue forecast to USD 1.15tn and NAND to ~419bn: Chinese CSPs scaling back 2027 orders since mid-November, trimming non-LTA server DRAM since early October; LTAs 'hold while prices flatten'
items.candidate_dial: memory-no-surface / B2-capex (the first forecaster to attribute the 2027 memory cut to a NAMED buyer class - Chinese CSPs - and to locate it OUTSIDE the LTAs, which is the query-5 distinction the sweep tracks: no renegotiation, but the uncontracted tail is being cut first; the China-order cut sits alongside the same week's export-control freezes (Nvidia SE Asia halt, Asian DC-loan freeze) as a China-channel, not a US-hyperscaler-channel, retreat; still a forecaster, not a principal - no hard event)
items.source: The Inference 'TrendForce cuts 2027 DRAM forecast to USD 1.15 trillion as China cuts orders, Micron and SK hynix carry the bill' (Richard Tang; 25 Nov 2026)

chips, equipment, computers, phones, networking proposed exempt; hearing 25 Jan 2027, no effective date); ASML and Infineon each >+3%; Imperial Brands +13.3% (Altria approach); Tokyo: Kioxia +14.5% intraday to 7,895 (close +8.86% per widget; AP 57,768.92); RATES (Saxo, futures-implied, US cash closed): UST 10y 4.918% (+~6bp), 30y 5.305% (+~6bp), 2y 4.685% (+4bp), 2s10s 23bp (-6bp w/w); Gilt 10y 5.16% (+~2bp); Bund up, no level; VIX 26.80 overnight, Dec future 23.73 (backwardation; skew 142.06; VIX1D had jumped ~two-thirds to 39.36 Wed; options price 1.37% for Friday's half-session, 3.2% into 4 Dec, the Dec contract spanning the 8-9 Dec FOMC); MOVE <100; EUR 1.0980, USD/JPY ~159.35 (MoF: ready to act with the US Treasury); BoJ's Tamura: another hike to be discussed in December or later; gold ~3,660 (+2.6%; 3,427 Wed low), silver 44.30 (+6.6%), copper +~5% (biggest in ten months) after China's State Council pledged to stabilise markets; Bitcoin ETFs record USD 5.39bn November outflow; BANK OF ENGLAND FSR / FPC record (26 Nov): FPC proposes a 30bp cut to UK bank capital requirements; AI financing - hyperscaler bond issuance expected >USD 305bn in 2026 (~8% of global IG, higher with other AI issuers), funding spread across equities, public bonds, private credit and 'complex structures including circular financing tied to future revenue commitments' that can obscure concentrations, makes it more likely that 'financial stress will spread between markets'; stretched valuations with sharp post-midterm AI-share falls; hedge funds reducing borrowing amplified moves and in a severe shock global investors could cut leverage in other markets 'including sovereign debt'; US CCC and lower-quality AI-related spreads widened sharply, higher-rated more limited; MPC's Greene: rates may need to rise faster if the Middle East conflict persists; Bloomberg (26 Nov): BoE to proceed with gilt-repo reform next year as hedge-fund leverage raises risks (headline only, refused host); Saxo: Commerzbank reviewing a reduction in US Treasury trading, possibly exiting the US repo market; ANT: no trade; 82.79 Wed close (second session below the 83 offer; 73.85 Wed low ~USD 987bn on 13.37bn shares), lock-up release of up to 303m shares from 15 Dec
